tasks.short: Choose tests, fill in order forms, perform the ECG, watch for results, interpret them and record the interpretation and plan.

steps.what: Nurse practitioner decides which diagnostic tests to order
Nurse practitioner fills in lab and imaging order forms with patient data and indication
Nurse practitioner performs the electrocardiogram
Nurse practitioner checks the lab portal several times a day for incoming results
Nurse practitioner interprets the results of blood counts, ECGs and x-rays
Nurse practitioner records the interpretation and plan in the record

tasks.design: Order sets in the electronic health record ({OTHER}) prefill patient data and common indications, so an order takes a few clicks. Results arrive in a result inbox that flags values outside fixed reference ranges and shows earlier values beside them, so the practitioner no longer checks the lab portal. A note template pulls the results into the record and the practitioner adds the interpretation; choosing tests, performing the ECG and interpreting stay with the practitioner, and no AI reads results.
tasks.previous_blocker: Orders were typed in full and results were found by checking a separate portal.
tasks.enabler_now: Order sets, result inboxes with reference-range flags and note templates are standard record functions.
tasks.still_hard: Flags only follow reference ranges; what a result means for this patient is judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that a normal blood count does not fit how ill the patient looks.

reach.learn: Whether flagged inboxes shorten result handling.

evidence.claim: Record systems offer order sets, result inboxes with reference-range flags and note templates.
Solely automated care decisions need a legal basis under GDPR article 22(2); flags only sort results for the practitioner.

assumptions: Boundary: from test choice to the recorded interpretation; treatment is outside.
Input contract: results sent by the hospital lab and imaging department; reference ranges set by the lab; order sets agreed by the medical staff; fallback is the lab portal.
Choosing, performing and interpreting do not change.
Lab staff time is outside the practitioner's savings.
research_questions: Are abnormal results acted on sooner?

incremental.description: Nurse practitioner learns the order sets and inbox.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Practices that already use order sets save less.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Explain self-management in the consult, find vetted patient pages, write tailored instructions, send them through the portal and answer follow-up calls.

steps.what: Nurse practitioner educates patients about self-management of their illness in the consult
Nurse practitioner looks up and prints patient leaflets on the illness
Nurse practitioner writes instructions tailored to the patient's individual circumstances

loop.input: The practitioner's consult note, the care plan values in the record and the vetted patient pages for the diagnosis.
loop.output: Plain-language instructions for this patient, each advice line citing the vetted page paragraph or the care plan entry it comes from.
loop.check: Code copies medicines, doses and targets from the care plan, never from the model, and checks every advice line cites a vetted paragraph or plan entry; the practitioner edits and approves every text.
loop.stop: One draft per consult; on failure the practitioner writes the instructions.
loop.why_not_simpler: Tailoring general advice to one patient's plan and words needs free text; a fixed leaflet cannot do it.

steps.what: Nurse practitioner prints or e-mails the instructions and leaflets to the patient
Nurse practitioner answers patients' follow-up questions by phone

tasks.design: The electronic health record ({OTHER}) links each diagnosis code to vetted, guideline-based patient pages. After the consult, a bounded step drafts tailored instructions from the consult note, the care plan values and those pages; the practitioner edits and approves them, and only then does the patient portal send them with the page links. Teaching in the consult and phone follow-up stay with the practitioner; no chatbot advises patients.
tasks.previous_blocker: Instructions were written by hand and leaflets looked up and printed per patient.
tasks.enabler_now: Vetted, guideline-based patient information exists, and language models can draft plain text from a plan with citations.
tasks.still_hard: Wrong advice can harm; doses and targets must come from the plan, not the model.
tasks.human_edge: Finding the one change a tired patient will actually make.
tasks.altitude: The practitioner approves drafted instructions instead of writing them.

reach.learn: Whether tailored written instructions cut follow-up calls.

evidence.claim: Thuisarts offers guideline-based patient information written with GP and specialist associations and the patient federation.
Providers are responsible for careful use of generative AI: assess risks, test and monitor.
Health data are special category; expect a DPIA.

assumptions: Boundary: from the consult to follow-up questions; changes in treatment are outside.

Input contract: diagnosis codes and care plan values recorded by the practitioner in the record; vetted patient pages from the national patient information site under its terms; fallback is printed leaflets.
Teaching in the consult does not change.
Patients' reading time is outside the practitioner's savings.
unknowns: Share of patients who use the portal.
research_questions: Do follow-up calls fall with tailored written instructions?

already_counted.description: Nurse practitioner edits and approves each draft.

incremental.description: Nurse practitioner checks the page links per diagnosis once a year.

approvals.approved_version: The instructions as edited and approved by the practitioner in s3; any change needs a new approval before sending.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Patients without the portal still get printed sheets.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Scan sources for changes, read changed rules in full, look up answers to practice questions and attend training.

steps.what: Nurse practitioner scans newsletters and websites for changes to regulations and reimbursement rules
Nurse practitioner reads the changed rules in full
Nurse practitioner searches laws and tariff rules to answer a practice question

loop.input: The practitioner's question and the indexed current texts of Dutch health laws and the healthcare authority's tariff rules.
loop.output: An answer quoting the relevant article or rule with its link and version date.
loop.check: Code checks that every quote matches the source text word for word and comes from the current version; the practitioner reads the quoted source before acting.
loop.stop: One answer per question; no matching source means the answer says 'not found'.
loop.why_not_simpler: Keyword search over laws and tariff rules returns too many hits for a busy clinician.

steps.what: Nurse practitioner attends accredited training and peer meetings on practice rules

tasks.design: A feed collects new versions of the laws, tariff decisions and professional guidance that apply to the practice from official sources ({GOV_PORTAL}) into one weekly list with links, replacing the scan of newsletters. For practice questions, a bounded step answers only by quoting the current law or tariff text with its link and date, and the practitioner reads the source. Reading changes in full and training stay as they are.
tasks.previous_blocker: Changes were spread over newsletters and sites, and questions meant long searches.
tasks.enabler_now: Laws and tariff decisions are published online with version dates, and language models can match a question to a passage.
tasks.still_hard: Rules interact; a quoted article can miss an exception elsewhere.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing when a question needs the professional association or a lawyer.

reach.learn: Whether the weekly list replaces separate newsletters.

evidence.claim: Dutch laws are published online with version dates.
A prescription must come from a named practitioner; AI drafts, it does not prescribe.
Providers are responsible for careful use of generative AI: assess risks, test and monitor.

assumptions: Boundary: from changes and questions to knowledge maintained; changes to practice protocols are outside.
Input contract: source list of laws, tariff decisions and guidance set by the practice manager; fallback is newsletters and search.
Reading in full and training do not change.
research_questions: How often does the practitioner need a source the tool did not find?

already_counted.description: Nurse practitioner reads the quoted sources.

incremental.description: Practice manager keeps the source list current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Changes that need full reading and training do not shrink.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Take the lifestyle history, discuss motivation, recommend interventions and agree goals, write and send the referral and record goals.

steps.what: Nurse practitioner takes the lifestyle history with standard questions
Nurse practitioner discusses motivation and options with the patient
Nurse practitioner recommends interventions to modify behavior and agrees goals
Nurse practitioner writes the referral letter to the lifestyle programme
Nurse practitioner e-mails the referral to the programme
Nurse practitioner records the goals in the care plan

tasks.design: Patients fill in a standard lifestyle questionnaire in the patient portal before the visit, and the answers appear in the electronic health record ({OTHER}), so the practitioner asks only follow-up questions. A referral template fills patient data, history and agreed goals from the record; after the practitioner checks it, it goes by secure care messaging. Goals are recorded with pick lists. Discussing motivation and recommending interventions stay in person.
tasks.previous_blocker: The history was taken question by question and referrals were typed and e-mailed.
tasks.enabler_now: Patient portals carry questionnaires into the record, and referral templates fill from it.
tasks.still_hard: Patients answer questionnaires optimistically; the talk still tests them.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing what really stops a patient from changing.

reach.learn: Whether structured referrals start coaching sooner.

evidence.claim: Patient portals carry questionnaires into the record, and referral templates fill from it.
Solely automated care decisions need a legal basis under GDPR article 22(2); this design keeps the decision with the practitioner.

assumptions: Boundary: from the lifestyle history to the referral and recorded goals; the programme itself is outside.
Input contract: lifestyle questionnaire filled in by the patient in the portal; questionnaire and referral template set by the practice's medical staff; fallback is asking in the consult.
Discussing and recommending do not change.
Patients' time is outside the practitioner's savings.
unknowns: Share of patients who fill in the questionnaire.
research_questions: Do referred patients start the programme more often?

already_counted.description: Nurse practitioner reads the questionnaire before the consult.

incremental.description: Nurse practitioner learns the referral template.

approvals.approved_version: The referral letter as checked by the practitioner in s4; any change needs a new check before sending.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Patients who skip the questionnaire save nothing on the history.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The nurse practitioner keeps diagnosis, teaching and every clinical decision; orders, result chasing, leaflets, searches and letters shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A practitioner who spends the saved time with patients who need longer talks.
